raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

Large CUDA k-pool prefills repeat the indexer logits and top-k work on every attention TP rank. Split the query rows across ranks and gather the selected indices.

## Modifications

Add `SGLANG_OPT_USE_DSA_KPOOL_PREFILL_TP=1`, off by default, for large eager CUDA prefills using the k-pool extend plan. Each rank processes its rows within the existing memory-budget chunks and gathers int32 indices, preserving -1 padding.

Context parallelism, scattered inputs, graph capture/replay, empty key pools, small batches and the unplanned path keep the existing behavior. Every TP rank must select the same path because it adds a collective.

## Accuracy Tests

CPU row-sharding, scheduling and environment suites pass, along with scoped formatting and registration checks. The production-selector check stubs the gather, so it does not validate NCCL or GPU numerics.

An earlier TP4 B200 NCCL check of the row-chunk method matched the replicated result for uneven rows, chunk boundaries, page-table mappings and padding. That check predates this PR head. Earlier full-model measurements combined other changes and do not establish accuracy for this branch.

Run the focused CPU suites with `python -m pytest`. Full-model accuracy on the current PR commit is still required before merge.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

An earlier v0.5.20 backport on TP4 B200, GLM-5.3-Flash FP8 and other serving patches measured a 44K-token prefill behind 60K cached tokens. Interleaved sharded and replicated indexer runs averaged 1.0354 s and 1.0878 s respectively, a 4.8% reduction. Warm-server variation was about 0.3% to 1.1%; restarts moved baseline latency by about 2.5%.

These are backport measurements. Accuracy and speed on this exact PR commit, TP8 and other GPUs remain unvalidated.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

## Review and Merge Process

Related: #42977 applies row sharding to Ascend/NPU.

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).
2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers.
3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.
   - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci`
4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR.

         assert topk_result is not None

@@ -0,0 +1,16 @@
+"""Partition replicated indexer rows without changing their global row indices."""
+
+
+def shard_row_chunks(
+    row_chunks: tuple[slice, ...], world_size: int, rank: int
+) -> tuple[tuple[slice, ...], int]:
+    num_rows = row_chunks[-1].stop
+    rows_per_rank = (num_rows + world_size - 1) // world_size
+    start = rank * rows_per_rank
+    end = min(start + rows_per_rank, num_rows)
+    chunks = tuple(
+        slice(max(start, chunk.start), min(end, chunk.stop))
+        for chunk in row_chunks
+        if max(start, chunk.start) < min(end, chunk.stop)
+    )
+    return chunks, rows_per_rank * world_size

@@ -0,0 +1,34 @@
+"""Query sharding must preserve global row order across memory-budget chunks."""
+
+import unittest
+
+from sglang.srt.layers.attention.dsa.prefill_tp_rows import shard_row_chunks
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cpu_ci
+from sglang.test.test_utils import CustomTestCase
+
+register_cpu_ci(est_time=1, suite="base-a-test-cpu")
+
+
+class TestPrefillTPRows(CustomTestCase):
+    def test_chunks_reassemble_without_missing_or_duplicate_rows(self):
+        for num_rows in (8, 17, 4097, 16384):
+            for world_size in (2, 4, 8):
+                for chunk_size in (3, 1024, 16384):
+                    chunks = tuple(
+                        slice(i, min(i + chunk_size, num_rows))
+                        for i in range(0, num_rows, chunk_size)
+                    )
+                    all_rows = []
+                    for rank in range(world_size):
+                        local, padded = shard_row_chunks(chunks, world_size, rank)
+                        rows = [
+                            i for chunk in local for i in range(chunk.start, chunk.stop)
+                        ]
+                        self.assertLessEqual(len(rows), padded // world_size)
+                        self.assertEqual(padded % world_size, 0)
+                        all_rows.extend(rows)
+                    self.assertEqual(all_rows, list(range(num_rows)))
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()

@@ -520,6 +520,61 @@ def _chunking_patches(*, rows_per_chunk, kv_pool, rocm=False):
         yield
 
 
+class TestKPoolTPChunking(CustomTestCase):
+    def test_shard_preserves_row_metadata_and_output_padding(self):
+        n_real, world_size, width = 17, 4, 4
+        pool_lens = torch.arange(1, n_real + 1, dtype=torch.int32)
+        expected = _expected_rows(
+            pool_lens=pool_lens, index=torch.arange(n_real), width=width, pad_rows=5
+        )
+        for rank in range(world_size):
+            calls = []
+            backend = _chunk_backend(topk=_encoding_topk(width=width, calls=calls))
+            group = SimpleNamespace(
+                world_size=world_size, rank_in_group=rank, device_group=object()
+            )
+            per_rank = (n_real + world_size - 1) // world_size
+
+            def gather(output, local, *, group):
+                start = rank * per_rank
+                stop = min(start + per_rank, n_real)
+                torch.testing.assert_close(local[: stop - start], expected[start:stop])
+                if stop - start < per_rank:
+                    self.assertTrue(torch.all(local[stop - start :] == -1))
+                output[:n_real] = expected[:n_real]
+
+            with (
+                _chunking_patches(rows_per_chunk=3, kv_pool=object()),
+                patch.object(
+                    torch.distributed, "all_gather_into_tensor", side_effect=gather
+                ),
+            ):
+                actual = backend._kpool_topk_by_row_chunks(
+                    q_fp8=_fp8_zeros(n_real, 4),
+                    weights=torch.arange(1, n_real + 1, dtype=torch.float32).reshape(
+                        n_real, 1
+                    ),
+                    kv_fp8=(_fp8_zeros(16, 4), torch.ones(16, 1)),
+                    logits_starts=torch.zeros(n_real, dtype=torch.int32),
+                    logits_ends=torch.full((n_real,), 16, dtype=torch.int32),
+                    pool_lens=pool_lens,
+                    seq_lens=pool_lens,
+                    page_table=None,
+                    page_table_row_index=None,
+                    topk_offsets=torch.arange(n_real, dtype=torch.int32),
+                    topk_row_starts=torch.zeros(n_real, dtype=torch.int32),
+                    row_chunks=_row_chunks(
+                        num_rows=n_real,
+                        num_cols=16,
+                        device=torch.device("cpu"),
+                        rows_per_chunk=3,
+                    ),
+                    out_rows=n_real + 5,
+                    tp_group=group,
+                )
+            torch.testing.assert_close(actual, expected)
+
+
 class TestKPoolPlanChunking(CustomTestCase):
     NUM_REQ_SLOTS = 64
     TOPK = 4
